scope: Full agent-first acceptance research for ClawX: software engineering acceptance, engineering evidence methods, Anthropic agent-era evaluation, and automated surrogate review. Planning and source research only; no candidate acceptance claim.

providers.name: AnySearch
providers.use: broad discovery and authoritative URL extraction

providers.name: Exa
providers.use: semantic source selection and source-grounded highlights

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1:2022 General concepts
sources.use: Risk-based testing, test levels, test basis and oracle, independence, configuration and test completion.
facts: The standard explains that exhaustive testing is impractical and requires sampling.
It defines test basis and test oracle as core acceptance inputs.
It describes unit/component, integration, system, system-integration and acceptance test levels.
It identifies the benefits of test independence.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-2:2021 Test processes
sources.use: Organizational, management and dynamic test processes.
facts: Defines generic testing processes applicable across lifecycle models.

sources.title: TMMi Framework model V2.0
sources.use: Entry/exit criteria, risk-based approach and test completion.
facts: Test entry criteria include environment and test documentation readiness.
Exit criteria measure executed/passed tests, coverage and summary reports.
Test approach must be revised when product risks or priorities change.

sources.title: Playwright best practices
sources.use: Isolated tests, observable locators and independent state.
facts: Each test should run independently with isolated local storage, session storage, data and cookies.

sources.title: Playwright Electron automation
sources.use: Launch and exercise the real Electron main process and renderer.
facts: Electron automation can launch the application and access its main process and windows.

sources.title: The Practical Test Pyramid
sources.use: Layer tests by granularity/cost while retaining system coverage.
facts: Fast granular tests and slower end-to-end tests detect different failures.

sources.title: Contract Test
facts: Consumer-driven contract testing checks expectations at integration boundaries.

sources.title: Compliance in a DevOps culture
sources.use: Property, measurement, evidence, constraint and validation as an evidence model.
facts: Compliance evaluates measurable system properties and validates evidence against constraints.
The evidence and validation result should be recorded.

sources.title: fast-check property-based testing
sources.use: Invariant and generated-edge-case testing with reproducibility.
facts: Property tests generate inputs to seek violations of invariants.

sources.title: StrykerJS mutation testing
sources.use: Measure whether tests detect intentionally introduced defects.
facts: Mutation testing injects defects and measures whether tests catch them.

sources.title: OWASP Developer Guide: Static Analysis
sources.use: SAST in CI with explicit blocking policy and false-positive handling.
facts: SAST findings are candidates requiring risk-context review and a project-defined gate.
SAST can have false positives and false negatives.

sources.title: OWASP Smart Contract Security: SDK testing gates
sources.use: Independent CI gates for static analysis, dependency scanning, SBOM, secrets and provenance.
facts: Security controls should be independent gates tied to defect classes.
Tests should avoid live production credentials and undeclared network.

sources.title: OpenSSF Open Source Project Security Baseline
sources.use: Automated test and security baseline before changes are accepted.
facts: Projects should run automated suites in CI before merging into the primary branch.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.use: Canonical agent evaluation model and lifecycle.
facts: Agent evaluation distinguishes tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, final environment outcomes, the evaluation harness, agent harness and suites.
Each trial should start from a clean, isolated environment.
Prefer deterministic graders, then model graders when needed; use human review judiciously.
Grade outcomes first and paths when safety, evidence or contracts require it.
Capability evals, regression evals and negative behaviors need balanced coverage.
Initial suites can start with 20-50 realistic tasks drawn from actual failures.
A task should be unambiguous, solvable, and have a reference solution where feasible.
A 0% pass rate over many trials is often evidence of a broken task or grader.
LLM judges should use structured rubrics, per-dimension isolation and an explicit unknown result.
Trials need repetition because agent outputs vary; aggregate with pass@k or pass^k as appropriate.
Reports should include tool calls, runtime, token use, errors and transcript inspection.
No single evaluation layer catches everything; use layered evidence.

sources.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
sources.use: Resource and infrastructure controls for agent benchmarks.
facts: The runtime is part of the agent problem-solving loop, not a passive container.
Two agents with different resource budgets and time limits are not taking the same test.
On Terminal-Bench 2.0, resource configuration changed results by up to 6 percentage points (p < 0.01).
Infrastructure errors ranged from 5.8% under strict enforcement to 0.5% uncapped.
A guaranteed allocation and a separate hard ceiling are needed instead of one pinned value.
Resource headroom should be calibrated so scores at floor and ceiling remain within noise.
Each trial must start isolated; shared state creates correlated failures or unfair learning.

sources.title: Harness design for long-running application development
facts: The harness used planner, generator and evaluator agent roles.
Generator and evaluator negotiated each sprint contract before implementation.
The evaluator clicked through the running application and graded functionality, visual design and code quality.
Each criterion had a hard threshold; a failed threshold returned the sprint for repair.
File artifacts carried context and negotiation between agents.
Different agent roles addressed distinct failure modes rather than adding parallel self-reviews.

sources.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.use: Persistent task state, incremental work and end-to-end verification.
facts: Initializer and coding agents used structured feature lists, progress files, git history and an init script.
Every later session reads durable state and runs a basic end-to-end check before new work.
Agents mark a feature complete only after end-to-end verification.
A clean, mergeable environment is an acceptance condition.
Browser automation improved end-to-end defect detection beyond source inspection.

sources.title: Designing AI resistant technical evaluations
sources.use: Task quality for complex and long-horizon work.
facts: Tasks should represent real work and provide high signal.
A good evaluation should not hinge on a single insight and should give many chances to demonstrate ability.
The scoring distribution should be wide enough to differentiate performance.
Realistic tooling, comprehension time and longer time horizons can improve validity.
AI-assisted work can be evaluated while still requiring substantive technical performance.

sources.title: A statistical approach to model evaluations
sources.use: Repetition, paired comparisons, confidence intervals and power analysis.
facts: Repeated samples help account for stochastic model output.
Paired differences remove variance attributable to shared question difficulty.
Confidence intervals quantify uncertainty around observed scores.
Power analysis relates sample count, false positives and detectable effect size.
A suite too small for the desired effect can only report a wide interval or insufficient evidence.

findings.finding: Acceptance needs one task specification and one explicit oracle before a candidate is run.
findings.implication: Each TF child must name its inputs, command, expected final state, negative control and artifact.

findings.finding: A deterministic final state must control the verdict whenever one exists.
findings.implication: Model graders supplement code/state oracles and return unknown when evidence is insufficient.

findings.finding: Agent nondeterminism, environment variance and nondeterminism require repeated trials and uncertainty reporting.
findings.implication: Core quality claims need trial counts, confidence intervals, paired comparisons and resource fingerprints.

findings.finding: A zero pass rate is a task/grader defect signal until a reference solution or feasibility proof says otherwise.
findings.implication: Task calibration is a required acceptance node; bad tasks do not count as agent failures.

findings.finding: Independent agent roles are useful when they have distinct evidence responsibilities; extra self-review is not.
findings.implication: Use planner/executor and independent verifier/evaluator with separate actors and worktrees.

findings.finding: Human review is not required for first-line acceptance under repository policy.
findings.implication: Automate UI actions, transcript review, qualitative rubric judgment and verdicts; label them agent-driven.

findings.finding: Source, runtime, effect, package, operations, agent quality and release approval are separate claims.
findings.implication: The verdict schema must expose each dimension and preserve all product locks.

findings.finding: Infrastructure limits can exceed the difference between candidates.
findings.implication: Record CPU/memory floor and hard ceiling, network, timeouts, retries, worker count and infra error rates in the manifest.
Negative controls must exercise stale/tampered/self-approved/skipped/wrong-final-state and grader-bypass paths.

findings.finding: Capability and regression suites need different thresholds and maintenance.
findings.implication: A saturated capability eval graduates into regression; difficult tasks remain visible until calibrated.

boundaries: This research does not claim a current-candidate pass.
No real-human evidence is claimed or required.
No product lock, default, release state or publication status changes.
External source summaries are evidence for design and provenance; the linked source controls its claim.
Task Forest state remains local and must be changed only through the task-forest CLI.
